heroLead: Everyone knows Pompeys Pillar for the sandstone butte Clark carved his name into. Fewer people know what's on record under the river-bottom ground around it.
intro: The historic site draws the attention, but the working ground around Pompeys Pillar is Yellowstone River bottomland, mostly agricultural, with scattered conventional oil and gas history rather than anything resembling a defined field. If your family holds minerals near here, I treat them the way I'd treat any quiet rural parcel in this stretch of the county — checked against the actual recorded lease and production history, not against how well-known the landmark is.
The landmark's fame doesn't move the number one way or the other. What moves it is the recorded lease history, and I check that before I say anything about value.

sections.heading: River-bottom parcels and old severances
paragraphs: A good number of the interests I run into near Pompeys Pillar trace back to homestead patents along the Yellowstone River, with mineral rights severed off at some point when the land changed hands. Those chains can run through several owners before reaching your family, and I confirm each link before I make an offer.

sections.heading: What the activity record actually shows
paragraphs: I check for any lease of record, active or expired, and any nearby permitting activity through the state's records before discussing value. In this part of the county that record is usually thin, which shapes the offer honestly rather than inflating it.

faqs.question: Is there oil or gas production near the Pompeys Pillar landmark?
faqs.answer: The historic site itself has no bearing on mineral activity. Development in the surrounding river-bottom farmland has been limited and scattered.

faqs.question: My family's interest has been sitting unleased for a long time — is it still sellable?
faqs.answer: Yes. I buy unleased interests regularly, priced based on the actual record rather than assumptions.

faqs.question: How do you verify a river-bottom parcel's history?
faqs.answer: Through the recorded deed chain at the Yellowstone County Clerk and Recorder and a check of any state permitting activity nearby.

faqs.question: Does being near a historic landmark affect the value of my mineral interest?
faqs.answer: No. Landmark status doesn't factor into subsurface mineral value — I price the interest on production and lease history alone.

faqs.question: What's the first step if I want to sell a Pompeys Pillar-area interest?
faqs.answer: Send me the family name and whatever description you have of the parcel, and I'll pull the recorded chain to confirm what you hold before we talk numbers.
